'''Elisabeth Hagemann''' (born 6 Mar 1906 in [[Essen]],<ref  name="Tobies.2006"/> died 1989)<ref>{{DNB-IDN|1078257787}}</ref> was among the first female German [[mathematician]]s to obtain a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree.

== Life ==


Her parents were Otto Hagemann, a department director at [[Friedrich Krupp AG]], and Else Hagemann, née Clausius.
Elisabeth Hagemann got her [[abitur]] from the Victoria school Essen ([[:de:Viktoria-Gymnasium|de]]) on 6 March 1926.
She enlisted at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]] in spring 1926, then at the [[University of Bonn]] in spring 1928, where she got her [[Staatsexamen]] in [[mathematics]], [[physics]], and [[geography]] on 4 March 1932.<ref name="Tobies.2006">{{cite book | oclc=180937798 | url=https://www.mathematik.de/images/Mathematik/ALGORISMUS_58_2_ohne%20Abb.pdf | isbn=9783936905212 | author=Renate Tobies | editor= | title=Biographisches Lexikon in Mathematik promovierter Personen an deutschen Universitäten und Technischen Hochschulen WS 1907/08 bis WS 1944/45 | location=Augsburg | publisher=Rauner | series=Algorismus | volume= | edition= | date=Jun 2006 }} Here: p.140.</ref>

Then she worked as a school teacher in [[Bad Godesberg]], [[Bonn]], and [[Rhine Province]].
In May 1935, she became a [[research fellow]] (''[[Wissenschaftlicher Assistent]]'') of [[Otto Toeplitz]] at Bonn University.
On 28 Apr 1937, she obtained her Ph.D.<ref name="Tobies.2006"/><ref>{{cite thesis | type=Ph.D. thesis | author=Elisabeth Hagemann | title=Beitrag zum Reziprokentheorem in linearen Koordinatenräumen | institution=Rheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität | location=Bonn | year=1937 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=http://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007%2FBF01594168.pdf | author=Elisabeth Hagemann | title=Das Reziprokentheorem in beliebigen linearen Koordinatenräumen | journal=Mathematische Annalen | volume=114 | number=1 | pages=126&ndash;143 | date=Dec 1937 | doi=10.1007/BF01594168 }} Access at [http://www.digizeitschriften.de/dms/img/?PID=GDZPPN00227907X digizeitschriften.de]</ref> At that time, her main advisor, Otto Toeplitz, had already been dismissed due to the Nazi [[Civil Service Law]].<ref>{{cite journal|mr=0002797|last=Born|first=M.|author-link=Max Born|title=Obituary: Prof. Otto Toeplitz|journal=Nature|volume=145|year=1940|page=617|doi=10.1038/145617a0|doi-access=free}}, reprinted in {{cite journal|mr=0606137|last=Born|author-link=Max Born|first=Max|title=Professor Otto Toeplitz|journal=Integral Equations Operator Theory|volume=4|year=1981|issue=2|pages=278–280|doi=10.1007/BF01702386|s2cid=119380753}}</ref>
